newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI sees better '97 despite weak gold price.
newsitem.headline: JCI sees better '97 despite weak gold price.

text.p: South African mining group JCI Ltd said on Wednesday that it was likely to reap more profits in the current financial year, thwarting a weaker gold price and despite the cost of growing its asset base.

"Despite this and a weaker gold price, the sustainable earnings forecast for the financial year under current market conditions should show an improvement on the 1996 results," JCI said in a statement.
For the period ended December 31, JCI made 253 million rand in attributable profit, compared to 127 million rand previously.
JCI said it remained committed to its strategic objective of focus and operational growth.

The new ownership structure of JCI Ltd, in which Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd has agreed to sell its 34.9 percent stake in JCI to black empowerment consortium African Mining Group, was seen as a "very positive development".
"(It) should facilitate the company's strategy for further focus of its operations and support the opportunities for growth and enhanced efficiencies in these operations," JCI said.
